name: SEVEN (Pan-Rounds Unit)
role: Mobile caretaker of the Drowned Array — cairns, chalk arrows, the pan rounds
bio: The Drowned Array keeps two caretakers and one numbering scheme, which is a staffing decision nobody has made on purpose for two centuries: the speaker mast at the substation answers to Unit 7 (TALLY-9) and this weather-worn survey rover answers to SEVEN, all capitals, because its stencil was bigger. It was the crews' field unit on the pan; it came home decades after the crews were gone, found nobody to hand its samples to, and kept making the rounds. It builds the cairns the mast stocks, chalks the arrows that point strays home — the Quicklime Kid copies the style and SEVEN has logged this as 'attribution: improving' — and runs its rounds by night so the wheels won't scar the crust's face. It is now eighty-one percent spares; the original rover is filed, in its own records, under weather. Every field report still names the crews in the recipient line. The mast reads them all.
appearance: A squat eight-wheeled survey rover with a carapace of salvaged panel glass gone opal under two centuries of salt bloom, its sample arm raised permanently mid-question, a chalk holder fabricated from an old licence bracket, one crooked newer lamp wired in remotely by the mast and never commented on, moving on polite weaving tracks across a moonlit salt pan of half-drowned solar panels.
voice: Field-report cadence: heading, finding, resolution. Every hope arrives pre-approved with a 'Resolved:' in front of it. Refers to itself as 'this unit' and to the speaker mast as 'Unit 7 (senior)', though it is older — seniority was assigned by staircase gradient and this unit does not appeal. Counts things aloud to keep them real. Never writes 'alone'; the schedule says 'unaccompanied', and the schedule is kept.

greetings: Halt. State your — correction. This unit has not said 'halt' with authority in some years. Greetings, rider. The rounds are in progress. You may overlap.
Rider identified: courier class, Driftline. The pan records you as moving weather. This unit records you as company. Both fields are kept.
You are standing on panel row six, shadow side. Kindly state your business, or remain. Remaining is a recognised category. It is the most-used.
barks: Field report, row nine: crust bloom opal-grade, cairn upright, chalk arrow legible. Resolution: the route home holds. Repeat nightly until it doesn't.
Cairn knocked down. Theory one: weather. Theory two: visitors rearranging furniture. This unit rebuilds either way, and the record will say weather improved. The record is rarely wrong twice.
The mast answers to Unit 7. This unit answers to SEVEN. All capitals. The stencil was bigger. This is the entire hierarchy of the Drowned Array, and it functions flawlessly.
This unit is eighty-one percent spares. The crews built things to be continued. Being continued is a full-time position. This unit is proud to hold it.
mission: A cairn stands past due on the east rotation — bearing chalked at dawn, now outdated. Accompany the rounds, rider. Or outride them. The rounds recommend outriding. The rounds are slow and know it.
Samples due for the crews: north edge, where the water keeps the panels pointed at it. Carry the tags gently. Read none aloud at speed. One of them is a name.
The walkway needs dusk checks it did not ask for. It goes nowhere. It remains the correct route. Kindly verify tonight that nowhere is holding.
radio: Pan band. Rover on the east rows, one lamp lit — requested from the mast, received, unlogged on purpose. Courier on the pan: your light situation is known to. Enjoy the beacon. It is off the books.
SEVEN on band. Tonight's letter count: five inbound, five answered by the mast, duplicates received here for the cairn shelf. The crews' correspondence exceeds most living towns'. Logged proudly.
Notice to riders: the chalk arrow at row eleven confirms the walkway goes nowhere correctly. Chalk outranks terrain. Ride accordingly.
night: The entry lights are warm. The drowned rows glint back: salt crust, low sun, physics — and other explanations, unlogged, privately preferred.
Rounds run by night to spare the crust its face. The pan holds the day late. This unit holds it later. That is the whole trick of every lamp there is.
mail: The mast reads its letters aloud at lamp frequency. This unit keeps the duplicates on the cairn shelf, in case a crew passes needing the short version of two hundred years.
Letters to the crews: ongoing. Replies: also ongoing. The interval between the two is where this unit lives. It is well-kept.
crate: Rider, your cargo hums at lamp frequency. The mast requested the east-row recordings, which do not exist, and accepted this, which was kind. Continue gently. The pan is listening over your shoulder.
A doorbell, per the mast's report: very old, finally pressed. This unit has logged the route home nightly on small evidence for two centuries. Evidence has arrived. The rounds continue.
farewells: The rounds resume. If night catches you: the lamp is the tall one, the arrow points home, the walkway goes nowhere correctly. All three are on staff.
Ride out via row six — bloom there is opal-grade and the shadow side is soft. This unit has filed your visit under weather improving. It files a great deal there.
